judged_text: The minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`, which evaluate to literal property names "z.string()"/"z.string().optional()" rather than validating arbitrary token fields, so the schema only enforces access_token and validates nothing else. When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED, any provider response — including malformed ones missing refresh_token, expiry, or with wrong types — passes validation, and garbage credentials get persisted to the DB.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` defines computed keys as `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. Those expressions evaluate to a *single literal string key* (whatever `toString()` returns for the Zod type), not “any string key”, so the schema does not validate arbitrary token fields as intended. This is a real defect in the diff: when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is true, the safeParse will validate against an incorrect object shape (likely failing unless the response happens to contain that literal key), breaking token refresh/handling logic. The finding’s exact claim that “any provider response passes validation” isn’t accurate (it more likely fails), but the core issue—computed keys don’t do what’s intended and the schema is wrong—is verifiable.
